messages:
Julie (PM): Team, we need to lock a hard cut for the next milestone. My proposal: ship an MVP that supports text generation + streaming + basic auth/rate limiting so we can run customer pilots. Defer advanced multi-tenant routing, per-tenant policy rules, and the full admin UX to v1. Agree?
Mike (Eng): +1. Routing/filtering is a multi-week infra effort and is the biggest risk for the ship date.
Sara (Designer): I support deferring full admin UX. For pilots we can provide a simple invite-only toggle and read-only settings to make customers comfortable.
Tomas (QA): We'll need explicit acceptance criteria for pilots or we won't know when to call the milestone done.
Julie (PM): Draft pilot acceptance checklist below:
- Surface: text gen API + streaming responses + basic per-key rate limits
- Performance: p95 < 300ms on pilot traffic (default max_seq = 512 for pilot)
- Reliability: 5xx < 1% across pilot endpoints during canary
- Observability: token-level cost + per-route traces enabled for pilot orgs
- Regression: tokenization/output parity checks against golden prompts
- Customer validation: 2 customers complete the acceptance checklist
- Rollout: canary at 5% with automatic rollback to a fallback model variant
Mike (Eng): Achievable if we force default max_seq=512 and enable prefix caching. I'll add a pilot-only config flag to keep prod behavior separate.
Ravi (SRE): Canary and automated rollback are required. I'll implement failover to hosted fallback model and add SLO alerts for pilot orgs.
Tomas (QA): I'll produce a test matrix: 8 smoke tests + 3 perf scenarios + regression harness. ETA EOD today.
Julie (PM): Timeline decision: with this cut, pilot-ready in ~3 weeks. Trying to include routing pushes us ~2-3 weeks later and increases risk. Options: accept the scope cut and keep date, or keep scope and accept delay.
Sara (Designer): Can we ship a minimal admin page (read-only + invite flag) so we avoid support friction for pilots? Low effort, high signal.
Mike (Eng): Yep, I can scaffold the admin toggle in a day and wire it to route requests to the single-tenant path for pilot orgs.
Julie (PM): Plan B: if infra finds a blocking issue, run an internal dogfood pilot first and shift external pilot by one week. Prefer external pilot first for customer feedback.
Ravi (SRE): I'll draft the runbook for failover and incident steps specific to pilot orgs.
Tomas (QA): Add gate: regression parity for a representative prompt set (no semantic regressions).
Mike (Eng): We'll run the regression harness against the same model snapshot used in prod to surface diffs early.
Julie (PM): Ownership: Julie = product + customer comms; Mike = infra + rollout; Ravi = SRE/runbook; Tomas = QA matrix & tests; Sara = pilot UX.
Sara (Designer): I'll post the admin toggle mock in #design before lunch.
deploy-bot: Canary window tentatively scheduled: 2026-04-08 14:00 UTC -> 2026-04-08 18:00 UTC.
Mike (Eng): Request: default pilot seq=512 to reduce perf tail risk. Also need confirmation on whether any infra migrations (KV cache changes) block the 3-week ship.
Julie (PM): Approved: pilot default = 512. Mike, confirm infra PR status by EOD. If clear, we cut routing and proceed. If not, we'll escalate or take Plan B.
Tomas (QA): I'll include tests that validate 512 vs 1024 behavior and log any user-visible differences.
Ravi (SRE): For rollback prefer model-variant fallback, not full endpoint disable, to minimize customer impact.
Mike (Eng): Noted. Will validate rollback path in staging. :eyes:
Julie (PM): Thanks all. I'll update the milestone tracker and ping stakeholders after Mike confirms infra.
Sara (Designer): :thumbsup:
Tomas (QA): Posting test matrix here when ready.
Mike (Eng): Confirmed: no infra blockers from my side today. Proceed with scope cut.
